changed: bounded runtime metrics endpoint and dashboard panel
summary: Worktree Switcher now samples aggregate RSS and CPU for the complete Linux process group it owns, including package-manager, Next.js, and worker processes. Each runtime exposes current and peak RAM, CPU, process count, sample age, a bounded five-minute history, and explicit idle, stale, unavailable, or unsupported states.

The dashboard polls a lightweight authenticated metrics endpoint without repeating Git discovery. The same snapshot is available through read-only MCP status. Sampling runs only for active processes, stops with them, and never terminates a server; an optional CLI threshold adds a visual RAM warning.
title: Shipped managed server resource monitoring
validation: A Linux integration test started a detached parent with a worker child and verified that both members contributed to the process-group sample.
Process-manager tests verified current and peak RSS, CPU deltas, bounded history, configurable warning thresholds, explicit unsupported state, and no further samples after stop.
The lightweight metrics API test verified that polling does not call the dashboard or rediscover worktrees. Lint, TypeScript, all 64 tests, and the production build passed.
